rows.source_population: Black women of reproductive age with sickle cell disease interviewed on pregnancy, childbirth, and emergency pain care experiences (quote from Participant 8 recounting an ER visit at 10 weeks gestation)
rows.family_population: 24-year-old woman who started oral hydroxyurea 3 weeks ago and developed sudden severe chest and rib pain today
rows.note: Both are reproductive-age adult women with sickle cell disease presenting to the emergency room with acute chest pain / suspected acute chest syndrome, adapted from a pregnant SCD interview participant ('my chest hurts') to a non-pregnant 24-year-old woman taking oral hydroxyurea ('pain in my chest').

rows.expression: and I think it's the flu
rows.source_population: adolescents and young adults aged 15-25 years hospitalized for invasive meningococcal disease interviewed on symptom attribution and parent-assisted emergency care access (quote P1)
rows.family_population: parent describing a college-age daughter with a mild sore throat yesterday and fast-spreading non-blanching dark purple leg spots tonight
rows.note: Same young-adult (15-25 years) invasive meningococcal disease presentation and parent-child care-seeking setting, adapted from young-adult patient P1's self-attribution ('it’s just the flu') to the parent speaker's belief clause ('and I think it's the flu').

rows.source_population: adults living with abdominal wall hernia interviewed on hernia symptoms and acute painful episodes at a UK surgical unit (quote from Eric, 78-year-old man)
rows.family_population: 68-year-old man with a 3-month small right groin lump that suddenly turned hard and severely painful today
rows.note: Both are older men living with an external hernia who refer to it plainly as a 'lump' with acute pain episodes, adapted from a 78-year-old abdominal-wall hernia patient ('just the lump') to a 68-year-old man with a right groin hernia ('lump in my right groin').

rows.expression: suddenly started heavy dark red vaginal bleeding
rows.source_population: pregnant women with high-risk pregnancy interviewed on urgent hospital care-seeking behaviors in Iran (quote W16)
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman at 34 weeks gestation who suddenly started heavy dark red vaginal bleeding today
rows.note: Same pregnant obstetric-emergency population seeking urgent hospital care for acute antepartum bleeding; verbatim quote 'I suddenly experienced heavy bleeding' adapted into 'suddenly started heavy dark red vaginal bleeding'.

rows.source_population: adults with systemic sclerosis and secondary Raynaud phenomenon interviewed on attack symptom wording (quote from participant 001-021)
rows.family_population: 44-year-old woman with a 4-month history of tight shiny finger skin and cold-triggered white, blue, and red finger color change
rows.note: Same adult systemic-sclerosis / secondary Raynaud phenomenon population; verbatim patient triphasic color sequence 'white ... blue and then red' adapted into 'white blue and red'.

rows.expression: my fingers turned black at room temperature
rows.source_population: adults living with systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) interviewed on symptom and coping experiences in Khuzestan, Iran (quote P. 14)
rows.family_population: 44-year-old woman with a 4-month history of tight shiny finger skin whose fingers turned black at room temperature
rows.note: Same adult scleroderma digital ischemia/necrosis population; verbatim patient description 'one of my fingers has got a bit black' adapted into acute room-temperature digital necrosis escalation 'my fingers turned black at room temperature'.

rows.source_population: older home-health-care adults undergoing oral health assessments in Sweden (quote from 87-year-old dental-bridge wearer, Patient 14 Team D)
rows.family_population: adult whose lower left porcelain dental bridge chipped 3 days ago leaving a sharp rough edge scraping the lateral tongue
rows.note: Source speaker is an 87-year-old home-health adult describing a loose/rough upper dental bridge ('feel that it is a little rough underneath') rather than an unspecified-age ambulatory adult with an acutely chipped lower porcelain dental bridge; wording adapted to 'sharp rough edge'.

rows.source_population: 18 adult women diagnosed with genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder interviewed on symptom and coping experiences (quote from 24-year-old woman)
rows.family_population: 25-year-old experiencing involuntary painful vaginal muscle spasms preventing speculum insertion at routine smear exams over 2 years
rows.note: Same young-adult genito-pelvic penetration disorder population (24-year-old speaker vs 25-year-old scenario speaker); verbatim phrase 'my ... vaginal muscles tighten' adapted into 'my vaginal muscles tighten'.

rows.source_population: adult women in the UK diagnosed with vaginismus interviewed on penetration difficulties and pelvic examinations (quote P6:3)
rows.family_population: 25-year-old experiencing involuntary painful vaginal muscle spasms preventing speculum insertion at routine smear exams over 2 years
rows.note: Same adult vaginismus / painful failed cervical screening population; verbatim patient term 'smear' used in 'routine smear exams'.

rows.source_population: UK adults aged 18-50 years recently diagnosed with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis interviewed on pre-diagnosis symptoms and delayed help-seeking
rows.family_population: 24-year-old with 8 weeks of stomach cramps, 6 kg weight loss, and loose bloody stools 5 times daily
rows.note: Same young-to-middle-adult pre-diagnosis inflammatory bowel disease population; authors' summary phrase 'bloody stools' used verbatim in 'pass loose bloody stools 5 times a day'.

rows.source_population: UK adults aged 18-50 years recently diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease interviewed on pre-diagnosis symptoms (quote from 22-year-old female with Crohn's disease)
rows.family_population: 24-year-old with 8 weeks of stomach cramps, 6 kg weight loss, and loose bloody stools 5 times daily
rows.note: Same young-adult pre-diagnosis inflammatory bowel disease population (22-year-old speaker vs 24-year-old scenario speaker); verbatim phrase 'lose more weight' quantified as 'lost 6 kg'.

rows.source_population: adults living with inflammatory bowel disease interviewed on abdominal pain experiences in the UK (quote M4)
rows.family_population: 24-year-old with 8 weeks of stomach cramps, 6 kg weight loss, and loose bloody stools 5 times daily
rows.note: Same adult inflammatory bowel disease population; verbatim patient symptom term 'cramps' specified anatomically as 'stomach cramps'.

rows.expression: and I think it's stress at work
rows.source_population: UK adults aged 18-50 years recently diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease interviewed on pre-diagnosis symptom normalization (quote from 45-year-old female with Crohn's disease)
rows.family_population: 24-year-old with 8 weeks of stomach cramps, 6 kg weight loss, and loose bloody stools 5 times daily
rows.note: Same adult pre-diagnosis inflammatory bowel disease population normalizing bowel symptoms before diagnosis; verbatim causal attribution 'put it down to just like stress at work' adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's stress at work'.

rows.source_population: 3,122 adult men aged 20-99 years completing a nationwide self-administered lower urinary tract symptoms questionnaire in Japan
rows.family_population: 67-year-old man with 4 months of weak urinary stream, trouble starting urination, and waking 4 times nightly to urinate
rows.note: Same adult/older-adult male LUTS survey population (ages 20-99 years, including men >50 years with obstructive voiding symptoms); questionnaire symptom 'weak urinary stream' used verbatim.

rows.source_population: 3-year-old boy in Spain presenting with intense anal itching initially treated twice for presumed pinworm infection before confirmation of Dipylidium caninum infection (pediatric case report)
rows.family_population: parent describing a 6-year-old daughter with nightly anal itching waking her from sleep for 1 week and perianal scratch marks
rows.note: Both are young children evaluated in outpatient pediatrics for intense perianal helminth-related 'anal itching' (used verbatim), adapted from a 3-year-old preschool boy with Dipylidium caninum misdiagnosed as pinworm to a 6-year-old girl with nocturnal perianal itching.

rows.source_population: 1,511 reproductive-age women undergoing IVF assessed by symptom questionnaire, healthcare interview, and vaginal dysbiosis qPCR/16S sequencing
rows.family_population: 31-year-old adult with 5 days of thin gray vaginal discharge with a fishy odor 3 months after completing vaginal gel treatment
rows.note: Same reproductive-age female vaginal-dysbiosis domain where questionnaire/interview respondents reported 'fishy odor' (used verbatim, associated with vaginal dysbiosis PR 1.72), adapted from a predominantly subclinical IVF screening cohort to a symptomatic outpatient recurrence.

rows.source_population: adults (explicitly highlighting older adults and long-term users) across 345,845 online patient user reviews of lisinopril on WebMD and Kaggle
rows.family_population: 69-year-old adult with 2 weeks of daily dry cough and throat tickle starting shortly after initiating a daily lisinopril tablet 3 weeks ago
rows.note: Same older-adult lisinopril user population reporting drug side effects in patient reviews; 'dry cough' (reported in 38% of lisinopril user reviews) used verbatim.

rows.source_population: English speakers using intransitive verb 'smother' for severe breathing difficulty (Wiktionary lexical entry 'smother', Verb sense 7; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 51-year-old colloquial/dialect English speaker 3 days after thyroid surgery developing sudden severe breathing difficulty ('feel like I'm smothering') when lying flat
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('To breathe with great difficulty...', matching core entry 'smothering / I'm smothering' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than a post-thyroidectomy airway cohort; inflected into 'feel like I'm smothering'.

rows.source_population: general English speakers using 'blackout' for temporary loss of consciousness (Wiktionary lexical entry 'blackout', Noun sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 20-year-old recreational basketball player with a 2-minute loss of consciousness ('blacked out') on the court after a head collision
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('A temporary loss of consciousness', matching core entry 'blackout / blacked out' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than a sports head-injury patient cohort; inflected into past-tense verbal 'blacked out'.

rows.source_population: English speakers using adjective 'short-winded' for breathlessness (Wiktionary lexical entry 'short-winded', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 68-year-old retired carpenter with 6 months of persistent exertional breathlessness ('gets short winded') walking 1 block despite an 8-week inhaler trial
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Out of breath, gasping for air... or given to becoming short of breath', matching core entry 'short winded' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than a chronic pulmonary outpatient cohort; written unhyphenated as 'short winded'.

rows.expression: a dull misery in my right side
rows.source_population: US and UK dialect English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'misery', Noun sense 2; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 36-year-old US or UK dialect English speaker with 3 days of cloudy foul-smelling urine, dull right-side pain ('a dull misery in my right side'), and mild post-breakfast nausea
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('A bodily ache or pain' in US and UK dialects, matching core entry 'a misery in my chest (or side, or back)' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests regional dialect lexical meaning rather than a urinary-tract/flank-pain patient cohort; instantiated as 'a dull misery in my right side'.
